items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 14:1
items.html: The vocalization of Cholam, Tzere, Kamatz, Tzere in the simple names indicates the aspect of the illumination of the vessels themselves, for the simple HaVaYaH without the filling indicates the root of the degree, which is the aspect of the thin coarseness of the aspect of Keter, which coarseness is not yet sufficient for a coupling with the upper light from its own aspect, but must receive its lights from the upper one, and it is the aspect of the light of Nefesh, for the light of Nefesh clothes in the vessel of Keter. And therefore its vowels are like the movement of the letters: Cholam, Tzere, Kamatz, Tzere. The Cholam indicates the Haya and Yechida in it, which do not clothe in vessels, like the Cholam which is above the letters and not within them, for the letters are the vessels. And the Tzere indicates the aspect of the Hesed-Gevura in Bina, at the time when she is in the posterior toward Hochma, and therefore they are only two points: Hesed, Gevura. However, at the time when her posterior stops and she couples with Hochma, she is then discerned with the point of Segol, for the two upper points allude to HB, namely to Bina who couples with Hochma, and the third point indicates the Daat that couples them. And it is found that at a time when there is not yet a coupling of HB there, and there is in her only covered Hassadim, then there are in her no HB but only Hesed-Gevura, and they are alluded to by the Tzere, as above. And therefore the first Hey is vocalized with a Tzere, to indicate that there is not yet in her a coupling with Hochma, as explained. And therefore the Vav in the simple HaVaYaH is vocalized with a Kamatz, which indicates the Kamatz within ZA, for the Vav is ZA, as is known, and since it needs the illumination of Hochma and does not have it, because there is no longer any in Bina, as above, therefore the point of the Vav is with a Kamatz. And the last Hey is also vocalized with a Tzere, like the first Hey, which indicates the covered Hassadim, as above. And thus is explained the vocalization of the simple names, in which there is only the illumination of covered Hassadim, which are the aspect of the illumination of the vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 14:2
items.html: And it is known that these nine names in the three heads are from their inclusion one in the other, for the three heads are AB, SAG, MAH, where in the inclusion one in the other there are in each one three names, and therefore they are discerned: in the inner light, and in the surrounding, and in the upper surrounding, where the inner light is the Mocha Stima'ah, and the surrounding is the Mocha deAvira, and the upper surrounding is the Galgalta. And therefore the three names of the Galgalta are all AB, namely in the filling of Yodin, and in order to distinguish between what is from its own aspect and what it took from the lower ones below it by way of inclusion, the vowels come for this: for the HaVaYaH of its inner light, which it took from the inclusion in the Mocha Stima'ah, which is the aspect of Nefesh, there is no vocalization but on the simple letters alone, for the simple letters allude to the aspect of Nefesh, as above. And the second HaVaYaH, which it took from the inclusion in the air, which is the first surrounding, is vocalized in all its ten letters, meaning also in the letters of its filling. For the filling indicates the screen in it that couples with the upper light, and since here there is a coupling, for it is the aspect of the Mocha deAvira, therefore also the letters of the filling are vocalized, since this vocalization indicates a coupling in its own aspect, as above. And nevertheless the vocalization of the filling is not different from the vocalization of the simple name, for also the letters of the filling are vocalized with Cholam, Tzere, Kamatz, Tzere, like the simple, which indicates covered Hassadim, as above. And the inner light in the Mocha deAvira, in its own place, already has there a coupling of HB face to face, and the Tzere is there transformed into a Segol, as above; nevertheless here, in the place of the Galgalta, which is the aspect of the Mem of Tzelem, which does not receive Hochma, therefore there is no difference between the simple name and its filling, and also the filling is with Cholam, Tzere, Kamatz, Tzere, which indicates covered Hassadim, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 14:3
items.html: And the third HaVaYaH in the Galgalta, namely the aspect of its upper surrounding, is the aspect of the Galgalta itself, and therefore the letters of its filling are all vocalized with Kamatzim, for they indicate the aspect of the coupling in it, which is the aspect of Keter and Rosh, where there is a coupling of striking upon the coarseness in the screen that opposes clothing, and it is known that according to the strength of the opposition to clothing that is in the Rosh, so is the measure of the stature that expands for clothing in the body. And these two discernments are called Kamatz and Patach, for the force of striking that operates in Keter is called Kamatz, because it contracts the lights from coming into clothing; and the second discernment, namely the expansion in the body from above downward, is called Patach, from the term of the opening of the lights to come into clothing. And they are discerned as Keter and Hochma, for Keter is the Rosh and its point is Kamatz, and Hochma is the aspect of expansion from above downward, and therefore its point is Patach. And therefore all the letters of the filling in this HaVaYaH are with Kamatzim, since it is the aspect of Keter and Rosh. But the simple letters in the name are vocalized as the movement of the letters, which are Cholam, Tzere, Kamatz, Tzere, for they do not indicate the aspect of the screen and the coupling, but the aspect of the vessel itself, as above, and therefore their movement is like the movement of the letters, which are the illumination of the vessels. (Vol. 1, p. 313, Items 42, 43, 44).
